source_text: Si quis dicit Christum salvum factum esse, et non confitetur ipsum esse salvatorem mundi, ac lucem mundi, sicut scriptum est; anathema sit. Quo pacto potest quispiam dicere, Christum salvum esse factum? cum ipse Dominus dicat: Ego sum vita. Et: Ego veni, ut vitam habeant. Et: qui credit in me mortem non videbit; sed videbit vitam aeternam.
thought_title: Christ as life and savior versus made safe
orientation: Gregory condemns anyone who says Christ was made safe but does not confess him as savior and light of the world, citing the Lord's own words that he is life and gives eternal life to believers.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says Christ [to have been] made safe, and not confesses him [to] be savior of [the] world, and light of [the] world, as [it] is written; let him be anathema. By what pact can anyone say Christ [to] be made safe? since himself [the] Lord says: I am life. And: I came, that they may have life. And: who believes in me [he] will not see death; but [he] will see life eternal.

choices.why: salvus means safe, preserved, unharmed; the error is treating Christ as a recipient of salvation rather than the Savior himself
standard glossary rendering for salvator mundi; matches the creedal confession
direct citation of John 8:12; glossary term for lux mundi
Christ's own claim; predicate nominative without article in Latin
purpose clause with subjunctive; refers to abundant/eternal life
rejected: in order that they might possess life

choices.why: future indicative; Johannine language for escaping eternal death

bible_refs.note: Ego sum vita; qui credit in me mortem non videbit

pass_b_english: If anyone says that Christ was saved and does not confess that he himself is the savior of the world and the light of the world, just as it is written, let him be anathema. How can anyone say that Christ was saved? For the Lord himself says: I am life. And: I came that they may have life. And: whoever believes in me will not see death, but will see eternal life (John 11:25; John 10:10; cf. John 8:51, 11:26, 3:36).

problems.source_quote: Ego sum vita. Et: Ego veni, ut vitam habeant. Et: qui credit in me mortem non videbit; sed videbit vitam aeternam.
problems.why: John 8:12 ('light of the world') belongs to sentence 1, not these three quotes; the references are mismatched and omit John 8:51 ('not see death').
In Christian Latin, salvum fieri means 'to be saved' (contrasting directly with 'savior of the world'), not 'to be made safe'.
problems.ruling: salvum factum esse contrasts salvatorem mundi; salvum here is salvation, not physical safety.

problems.why: In Christian Latin, salvum fieri means 'to be saved', not 'to be made safe'; the theological contrast with 'savior' is lost.
problems.ruling: salvum esse factum repeats salvum/salvator contrast; made safe obscures saved-versus-savior heresy.
